attrs.evidence: Cited, not re-derived. THIS IS THE RULING R6 AND R7 BOTH ASKED FOR, delivered by GPT-5.6 on the second asking, and it is narrower than the question that was asked. Bloomfield, Netkachova & Rushby state that an uninvestigated or incomplete defeater causes the node it targets to be considered unsupported, that a refuted defeater is effectively removed from the primary case, and that accepted residual risk is a consciously retained state. THE R7.1 BINDING OF THIS CITATION WAS WRONG AND GPT-5.6 RULED SO: it mapped `uninvestigated or incomplete` onto both `open` and `sustained`, and the source distinguishes them — a sustained defeater is a CONFIRMED defect, and after repair it may be marked ADDRESSED and retained as commentary. All 21 sustained defeaters here reference fixed incidents, so the binding counted 21 repaired defects as live attacks. Corrected at R7.2 into a structured, well-definedness-checked map (ASR-BINDING-WELLDEFINED), in which `sustained` serves both source states separated by whether the repair currently holds — the predicate ASR-DEFEATER-TEMPORAL already derives. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE is whether the full typed Mosaic assurance graph compiles faithfully into the particular Dung framework being labelled — see ASR-COMPILE-AF, which stays OPEN and which GPT-5.6 explicitly declined to close on this basis.
